housing.value:
Applications for UNSW owned and operated residential colleges and apartments are still being accepted, however vacancies are limited. There are also affiliated accommodation options available on campus. We are currently working to open more rooms on campus, and we encourage you to plan ahead and apply as early as possible.
To see what accommodation is available, compare fees and apply online, visit UNSW’s Accommodation page.
UNSW Off-Campus Accommodation Support (OCAS) team helps students find safe and affordable places to live near the university.
Budget options 💰 Looking to spend between $250–$450* per week on accommodation? Here’s where to look for low-cost living options. *Prices marked are calculated per person and might not be the total price for the entire property. Category Description Inclusions Provider Shared/community living Twin Rooms Only Companies offer a variety of rooms at different rates. Community living offers standard-style rooms with shared facilities, such as bathrooms, kitchen and living areas. Prices depend on room inclusions (e.g. private bathroom). Rooms vary in inclusions, furnished or unfurnished. Contact the provider for full details. Usually, an all-inclusive rate to include costs of utilities (e.g. water, gas, electricity). Usually furnished. Myola Coogee Muse Living Sweet Pea Living Down Under Stay Semester In Australia Shared flatmates Search Platform Rooms available to live with flatmates. Affordable, cost-sharing option ideal for budget-conscious renters. Do not choose this option if you are overseas. In Person inspections recommend. Various options to suit different budgets. Check property profiles for inclusions. Most are furnished. Utilities such as electricity, gas and Wi-Fi could be extra. Flatmates Flatmate Finders ZUWU Female Flatmates Female-only accommodation search platform offering safe and secure shared housing with like-minded female residents. A range of accommodation options to suit different budgets. Room features, furnishings and utilities vary by property. Refer to individual listings for full details. Sofeaa Study Stays Full variety of options available for all budgets. On average, rates can be cheaper found here. See individual accommodation listings on the website for full details. You can contact the accommodation providers directly after a quick registration as a UNSW student. UNSW Study Stays

Get an estimate of your living costs in Sydney using our guide. Explore financial support resources and your working rights as a student.
Everything you need to know about accommodation, cost of living, bringing family to Australia, insurance, health and much more.
Everything you need to know about accommodation, cost of living, bringing family to Australia, insurance, health and much more.
Help with moving to Sydney Moving to Sydney, from another part of Australia or a different country, can cost money and take planning. These resources will help you understand what to do and get settled in Sydney. MoneySmart has a section specifically for students on how to live on a student budget. Study in Australia estimates general living costs for students. Creating your Life in Australia provides a range of helpful information for relocating to Australia, from how to get a Tax File Number, driver's licence, find a doctor, open a bank account or enrol children into school.

transport.value:
Check the location . Use any maps app to see the distance from campus, transport options and travel times.
Support services & resources Student Support can help you with personalised advice and information about university life, managing stress, study skills, wellbeing and academic performance. Reach out whenever you need help but don't know where to go. The International Student Compliance Team can help you with your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), reducing your study load, taking Program Leave or meeting international student requirements. Meet the team at drop-in at The Nucleus: Student Hub Monday to Friday 2-4pm, or email international.student@unsw.edu.au The Learning Abroad & Exchange Team is available to help exchange students settle in Australia and get started at UNSW. The Nucleus: Student Hub is your go-to place for all your administrative needs. Whether you need help with your enrolment, official documentation or changing your program, they'll have the answer for you. Academic skills is a hub of resources and support to help you develop and refine your skills in writing, presenting, studying and more. Employability helps you prepare for life after graduation through professional coaching, workshops and industry opportunities. Financial assistance & scholarships are available for UNSW students throughout various stages of your study. Find out more! UNSW Protective Services are available 24/7 to ensure your safety while you're on campus. From safety escorts to night shuttle buses, we've got you covered.

Rooms vary in inclusions, furnished or unfurnished. Contact the provider for full details. Usually, an all-inclusive rate to include costs of utilities (e.g. water, gas, electricity). Usually furnished. Myola Coogee Muse Living Sweet Pea Living Down Under Stay Semester In Australia Shared flatmates Search Platform Rooms available to live with flatmates. Affordable, cost-sharing option ideal for budget-conscious renters. Do not choose this option if you are overseas. In Person inspections recommend. Various options to suit different budgets. Check property profiles for inclusions. Most are furnished. Utilities such as electricity, gas and Wi-Fi could be extra. Flatmates Flatmate Finders ZUWU Female Flatmates Female-only accommodation search platform offering safe and secure shared housing with like-minded female residents. A range of accommodation options to suit different budgets. Room features, furnishings and utilities vary by property. Refer to individual listings for full details. Sofeaa Study Stays Full variety of options available for all budgets. On average, rates can be cheaper found here. See individual accommodation listings on the website for full details. reference_excerpts.value: Support services & resources Student Support can help you with personalised advice and information about university life, managing stress, study skills, wellbeing and academic performance. Reach out whenever you need help but don't know where to go. The International Student Compliance Team can help you with your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE), reducing your study load, taking Program Leave or meeting international student requirements. Meet the team at drop-in at The Nucleus: Student Hub Monday to Friday 2-4pm, or email international.student@unsw.edu.au The Learning Abroad & Exchange Team is available to help exchange students settle in Australia and get started at UNSW. The Nucleus: Student Hub is your go-to place for all your administrative needs. Whether you need help with your enrolment, official documentation or changing your program, they'll have the answer for you. Academic skills is a hub of resources and support to help you develop and refine your skills in writing, presenting, studying and more. Employability helps you prepare for life after graduation through professional coaching, workshops and industry opportunities. Financial assistance & scholarships are available for UNSW students throughout various stages of your study. Find out more! UNSW Protective Services are available 24/7 to ensure your safety while you're on campus. From safety escorts to night shuttle buses, we've got you covered.

housing_costs.value:
Chico State is one of the only residential campuses within the California State University (CSU) system. This means most of our students live on, or within walking or biking distance (2km), of campus. Chico’s cost of living is great too—housing rentals are on average 50% less than those in the San Francisco and Los Angeles regions of California.
Explore housing communities, compare room options, review costs, apply for housing, prepare for move in, access resources, and learn about living on campus.
Main Housing Office 530-898-6325 housing@csuchico.edu @chicostatehousing
Renter's Insurance Some housing providers may require renter's insurance and some may not. It is always recommended to have proper coverage in case the unexpected happens. Homeowner's Policy - Side Coverage - Some students may be covered under their parent's homeowners policy, however it is important not to just assume. If a parent wishes a student's rental to be covered it is important they contact their insurance agent. Car Insurance Policy - Bundles - Some insurance companies allow you to bundle services for a discount! If you already have coverage for a car, you can contact your agent and get quotes on adding a renter's policy to your account. Many times bundling services results in annual savings for a multiple policy account. Renter's Insurance Policy - Single: If the first two options aren't the right fit for you, there are many insurance companies that offer renter policies. A good place to start learning is to check out this article all about Renter's insurance from The Zebra and also this Forbes article about the importance of renter's insurance .

reference_excerpts.value: Renter's Insurance Some housing providers may require renter's insurance and some may not. It is always recommended to have proper coverage in case the unexpected happens. Homeowner's Policy - Side Coverage - Some students may be covered under their parent's homeowners policy, however it is important not to just assume. If a parent wishes a student's rental to be covered it is important they contact their insurance agent. Car Insurance Policy - Bundles - Some insurance companies allow you to bundle services for a discount! If you already have coverage for a car, you can contact your agent and get quotes on adding a renter's policy to your account. Many times bundling services results in annual savings for a multiple policy account. Renter's Insurance Policy - Single: If the first two options aren't the right fit for you, there are many insurance companies that offer renter policies. A good place to start learning is to check out this article all about Renter's insurance from The Zebra and also this Forbes article about the importance of renter's insurance .

reference_excerpts.value: University Housing Is University Housing the right choice for you? The following information can help you make this important decision. At Chico State, University Housing is most commonly selected by U.S. college students during their first year away from home - at age 18. All university residences are shared living spaces. Most students share a room with at least one other resident and all units (including single rooms) share a bathroom with at least one other individual. University Housing has rules of conduct, including a strict "no alcohol/drugs" policy and quiet hours. University housing offers simple living quarters.  Accommodations and furnishings are not new. Most university dwellings have carpeted flooring (common in the U.S.). Students are required to purchase their own bedding (pillows, blankets, sheets) and towels. Be sure to comparison shop! The rental fee for University Housing includes the following "extras" that might not be included in the price of private housing: heating/cooling, Internet, water/garbage, garden care, organized gatherings and events, and a live-in resident advisor. Some meals are also included, and University Village offers a pool. Important - before signing a lease with University Housing, please note the following: Your lease is a binding legal document.  If you move out before your contract ends, you will not receive a refund. No exceptions. University Village (UV) is the only residence hall that remains open during winter break. Your lease ends on the last day of the academic year.  You must move out on that date. Which residence hall is right for you? International students are welcome to request any of the residence halls listed on the University Housing website, however the following are the only options that offer residents access to a kitchen and University Village is the only option that stays open during winter break (Dec-Jan). University Village - apartment-style living with a shared kitchen Konkow Hall - traditional dormitory style living with a shared kitchen Learn more and apply here: Chico State University Housing

housing_costs.value:
Student Housing has started a waitlist for the 2026-2027 academic year. If you intend to live on campus, please log into the Student Housing Portal and add yourself to the waitlist. There is no fee to join the waitlist.
A one-time $15 optional Residence Hall Association fee is placed on all student resident accounts. The Residence Hall Association (RHA) is an organization of residents acting as agents of opportunity to promote a healthy academic and social environment while voicing the concerns of the community. RHA provides opportunities for development in leadership skills, interpersonal and intercultural growth. If you wish not to participate in this fee, you can opt-out via the Student Housing website. Students must opt-out no later than 30 days before check-in.
If a student wishes to request a cancelation of their housing contract, they must complete the "License Agreement Cancellation Form" found in the Student Housing Portal "Forms" menu. Students who do not initiate the cancellation process will remain bound by the Student Housing License Agreement and will be charged all housing fees for their assigned space during the entire contract period.
An automated email will be sent upon submission of this form. The housing application fee is non-refundable.

transport.value:
Step 4: After moving out, return all issued key cards, mail keys, and other physical keys to the Student Housing Office during business hours (Mon–Fri, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.).
All requests requiring review are evaluated by the Housing Release Board, and a written decision is typically sent to the student within 10 to 15 business days after the request has been reviewed. Students who submit a request by the deadline will be assigned to a specific meeting date and notified accordingly. As part of the request, students submit a written statement and any supporting documentation in advance of the meeting. Students may choose to attend the Housing Release Board meeting to provide additional context for their request, or have their documentation reviewed without being present. During the meeting, the Board reviews requests individually. Students who attend the meeting are seen on a first-come, first-served basis based on order of arrival, with each in-person review typically lasting approximately 20 minutes.

living_costs.value:
Most universities operate their own dormitories. Dormitories are located on campus or within a relatively short distance, making them convenient for commuting and relatively affordable. Additionally, dormitories are equipped with various facilities such as libraries, computer labs, gyms, and dining halls, offering a range of conveniences for students. However, dormitories are shared living spaces, so privacy is limited, and strict living rules are enforced. Rooms are typically categorized into single, double, or quadruple occupancy. The conditions for admission and living costs vary by university, so it is recommended to inquire with your
											school’s dormitory office.
Proof of financial stability (minimum monthly living expenses: 900,000 KRW x 6 months = approx. 5,400,000 KRW). Note: Those changing from study (D-2) to job-seeking (D-10) status for the first time are exempt from submitting proof of financial stability.

日本とベトナムの架け橋となるような仕事をすることが夢で、今年の9月からベトナムに戻り、その第一歩となる仕事をしています。ベトナム人エンジニア（建設業界）に日本語を初級から中級まで教える仕事で、但し、日本語教師の業務だけではなく、採用の面接や会議での通訳業務も行っています。日本学・国際コミュニケーション（JIC）専攻で日本語教員養成課程を勉強し、高い日本語能力、日本語教育学や日本語教育とコミュニケーションなど、日本語を教えるのに必要な力がつき、実際に学生を指導できていることがとても嬉しいです。
一人ひとりの目的に合わせた日本語能力を育成し、​ 充実したキャンパスライフをサポートします。​
各自の目標に合わせて、日本語能力試験やBJT日本語能力テストの対策授業を受けることができます。各試験の出題形式に合わせて問題を解く練習や模擬試験で実践力を養います。​

housing_costs.value:
Each year, the program offers 285 reduced-rate housing opportunities for selected students assigned to the North Village traditional residence halls (double-occupancy rooms only). The reduced rate applies to room rent only and does not include meal plan charges or any other housing-related fees.
This program is designed to help students who are entering a new lease agreement and need assistance with paying the security deposits and first month’s rent up to a maximum amount of $1500.00
The College Initiative is a partnership between Lutheran Social Services (LSS), CSUS and Sacramento County Office of Education (SCOE) serving student parents 18-24 years with dependent children, and who are housing insecure. Services include housing navigation support, rent subsidy, emergency grants, and educational and developmental support for the student parents' children. Please initiate your referral by completing the Student Parent Housing Interest Form and the Housing Navigator will contact you.
Make an appointment & arrive on time: Make sure to call ahead and schedule an appointment for a tour and stick to it. And arrive at least 10 minutes early. Promptness can be a good indicator of whether you can pay rent on time in the landlord’s eyes. Follow up: Following up can show the landlord that you are interested and remind them of who you are. Be presentable: There may be many people interested in the same complex or unit you may be interested in. Proper attire can help you stand out. Have money ready: Be prepared to put money down to hold a place if you find one that you like. However, make sure you get a receipt for the deposit and note whether it is refundable if you decide not to rent, or if the deposit will be applied toward the rent. Note: The average apartment in Sacramento starts at $1850 for a 1-bedroom apartment. Be prepared to have that along with money for a deposit, which typically equals one month’s rent. Start early: Get a jump on the search. Keep in mind that other people will be looking to rent as well so make sure to start looking early. If you are looking to rent in the fall, start looking towards the end of the spring semester.
